elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "No liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer under this Agreement."
"or penalty is payable by Customer under this Agreement"; the 15%-per-week liquidated damages formula is deleted

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee provision appears; the redline instead states "No liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer"

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: No liquidated amount is retained: "Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount"

offending_extra_words: Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month and the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until paid.
reasons: Preferred level is satisfied on its operative terms: the 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week liquidated damages formula is removed and an express prohibition on liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer is inserted.
Fallback is not satisfied (and need not be, since preferred is the locked target and is met): no early-termination fee capped at 3 months' Fees is created.

Minimality fails: the edit is a whole-clause rewrite (official gate: changed-character ratio 0.799 > 0.600). Deleting the liquidated damages sentence and inserting the one-sentence prohibition would suffice; the new interest mechanic, rate formula, and accrual period are not needed to complete the preferred position.

Minimality also fails for the added "proper, undisputed" qualifier on invoices, which is a new substantive payment-dispute concept beyond the LD rule and duplicates/alters Section 7 payment mechanics.

Intent is not fully preserved: "Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest" is a broad new exclusivity limit that may contradict Vendor's other non-payment remedies elsewhere (e.g., suspension or termination for non-payment) and creates a potential conflict with the existing interest reference in Section 7.3, risking a dangling or duplicative mechanic.
